note: The plugins a release took out of the stack, read by the Node seed alone. Update uninstalls each one only by its full spec - the name under the key the core is listed under (the 1.x key on a migrated install), or the `marketplace` its row names - so a same-named plugin from another marketplace (the official catalog ships a `sentry`) is never touched, and a row at another scope is kept and logged with its uninstall command. After each uninstall it prints the row's `addBack` line, `<scope>` replaced by the scope it went from. A row whose `addBack` reinstalls that same plugin (a third-party pick the stack dropped) goes on the first update past `retiredIn` only, while the last install's stamp predates it - from then on a row under that spec is the user's own, put back with that line (plugins.retirementDue). A cut MCP server is also named in the manifest's `retired.mcps`, which prunes a copy-route registration of it - only on the first update past `retiredIn`, because from then on a registration under that name is the user's own, made with this line. Its `registration` is what the stack itself registered (the package it launched, or the url it called): the prune removes only a registration of that shape, so a server the user added back under the name - with the addBack line or by hand - is kept. Keep a row while its name is retired: it is the only record of the way back.

plugins.name: ponytail
plugins.why: a third-party pick dropped in the 0.2.7x audit remediation - its SessionStart hook injected thousands of characters into every session

plugins.name: angular-cli
plugins.why: the MCP cut (R26) - framework tooling the Angular skills cover, loaded into every session of the projects that picked it
plugins.addBack: claude mcp add --scope <scope> angular-cli -- npx -y @angular/cli mcp

plugins.name: chrome-devtools
plugins.why: the MCP cut (R26) - playwright drives the browser, and this one needed a full Chrome on the machine
plugins.addBack: claude mcp add --scope <scope> chrome-devtools -- npx -y chrome-devtools-mcp@1.9.0

plugins.name: appium-mcp
plugins.why: the MCP cut (R26) - needed Xcode and/or the Android SDK plus Java, and no stack seeded it
plugins.addBack: claude mcp add --scope <scope> appium-mcp -- npx -y appium-mcp@1.94.3

plugins.name: sentry
plugins.why: the MCP cut (R26) - a hosted server with its own sign-in, which the stack only wrapped
plugins.addBack: claude mcp add --transport http --scope <scope> sentry https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp

plugins.name: context7-local
plugins.why: the MCP cut (R32) - context7 is the hosted server only; the local npx transport doubled its tool schemas beside it. A local-mode install printed a `/mcp disable context7` line: whoever ran it runs `/mcp enable context7` to switch the hosted one back on

plugins.name: claude-md-management
plugins.why: a third-party pick the plugins audit (2026-09-26) found unused - 0 uses in 230 sessions it was enabled in; the always-on habits-adjust-agents-md skill creates or improves an AGENTS.md and closes on a deterministic check, and a session's learnings belong in the shared memory server, not the file

plugins.name: security-guidance
plugins.why: a third-party pick the plugins audit (2026-09-26) scored a blocker - a billed model review of the diff per Stop, SubagentStop and commit with 0 findings in 217 sessions, sent under the user's own credential, and an unpinned pip install at every session start; /security-review, the security-auditor seat and the commit checkpoint's security half stay
